headline: Reverse three segments to rotate in place
statement: Rotate nums to the right by k positions, modifying the same list in place. k is nonnegative and may exceed the array length. The method returns nothing. Aim for linear time with constant extra space.
prerequisites: Basic Python lists, loops, and functions
intuition: Write the array as A+B where B is the last k values. Reversing everything gives reverse(B)+reverse(A). Reverse each segment separately to restore internal order, yielding B+A without allocating another list.
approach: Reduce k modulo the array length.
Reverse the entire list with two swapping pointers.
correctness: The first reversal swaps the segment positions and reverses their interiors. The next two reversals restore both interiors, producing exactly the last k elements followed by the first n-k. Modulo reduction preserves the rotation because a full n-step rotation is identity.
bruteForce: Move the final value to the front k times; repeated shifts cost O(n*k). An auxiliary rotated copy takes O(n) extra storage.

complexity.explanation: Three segment reversals collectively swap O(n) pairs. The helper uses two indices and swaps in the same list, with no slices or auxiliary rotated array.

pitfalls: Modify nums instead of returning a newly rotated list.
Reduce k before determining segment boundaries.
Avoid slices if claiming constant auxiliary space.
